The real deploy chain lives in a SEPARATE repo, Aspose/aspose.org-workflows: a daily cron (change-scanner.yml, 04:00 UTC) diffs aspose.org main against its last-scanned SHA, maps changed content paths to per-site workflows, and fires deploy-pipeline.yml with environment=staging first. deploy-status-checker.yml (triggered on workflow_run completion AND hourly cron) then AUTOMATICALLY re-fires the same workflows with environment=production once staging succeeds -- confirmed via `gh api .../environments` that BOTH the staging and production GitHub Environments have protection_rules: [] (no required reviewers, no wait timer). LIVE CONFIRMATION (2026-08-22, gh run list): the full pipeline fired today unattended -- Change Scanner 04:31 -> docs.aspose.org.yml staging build 04:32 (11m) -> production build auto-triggered 05:21 (11m), same same-day pattern on 08-18/08-19.

MATERIAL RISK FINDING surfaced by 0a, flagged to the user rather than silently absorbed into the rollout plan: once a canary (or any subdomain stage) is pushed to main, it is live in PRODUCTION within roughly 1-2 hours (one daily cron cycle away at worst, ~50 minutes staging-to-production once the cron fires), with ZERO human approval gate anywhere in that chain. RUNBOOK.md:441-468 confirms this deploy model is intentional/documented, not a bug. This means the plan's own Stage 1 approval checkpoint ('show before/after diff, wait for explicit approval BEFORE proceeding') is the ONLY human checkpoint that exists for real -- there is no second chance to review the canary on staging before it auto-promotes; the window to notice a problem and intervene (e.g. push a revert commit before the next cron cycle) is real but narrow.

STAGE 0b (rollback drill, executed for real, not simulated): ran backlink_backfill.py --write (real write mode, not dry-run) scoped via --files-from to exactly one real, low-stakes, already-known-non-canary content file (content/kb.aspose.org/en/pdf/cpp/_index.md -- a confirmed-live duplicate-link page tracked throughout this mission, deliberately NOT one of the actual cells/words canary targets). Confirmed the write executed for real (git diff showed a real 1-line change, matching the expected REPLACED_FAMILY_LINK fix). Executed the tool's own auto-generated rollback script (`git checkout HEAD -- <file>`) verbatim. Verified restoration via 3 independent methods: git diff (empty), git status (clean), and a raw non-git diff between git show HEAD:<file> and the working-tree file (exit code 0, zero output) -- byte count matched exactly (950=950 bytes) both before and after. One methodological false alarm during the drill: an initial raw SHA256 comparison appeared to mismatch, traced to comparing two differently-formatted hash outputs (sha256sum's own output line, which appends ' *filename', against a bare Python hexdigest) -- not a real discrepancy; the git-native and raw-diff checks are the authoritative confirmation and both passed cleanly. Entirely local -- nothing committed or pushed during the drill; confirmed via git status that the repo returned to its pre-drill state with zero residue.

Both 0a and 0b are documented here with evidence, per the card's own Stage 0 exit criterion. Per that same exit criterion ('human confirms understanding of the actual deploy/rollback mechanics before Stage 1 begins'), TC15 does NOT proceed to Stage 1 (the actual cells+words canary write+push) without the user's explicit go-ahead, especially given the newly-surfaced narrow no-human-gate auto-promotion window this stage was specifically designed to catch before it could surprise anyone mid-rollout.

title: Systematic content backfill: 5-stage safety-gated rollout (preflight, canary cells+words, per-subdomain staged rollout, re-audit, refresh-product exercise)
evidence_refs: STAGE 1 write-mode canary testing against real cells+words files surfaced 4 real bugs beyond anything Stage 0 planning anticipated, each found immediately after fixing the previous one (established mission pattern): (1) run_backfill()'s outer classify_compliance() call omitted existing_links/expected_anchor_text, so cells was silently skipped as 'Already COMPLIANT' despite live 'commercial edition' text -- fixed by computing existing_links2/expected_anchor_text2 and passing them. (2) backfill_products_yaml()'s OWN idempotency check had the identical blind spot one layer deeper (URL-presence-only) -- fixed by adding an anchor-text match requirement to that condition. (3) once both gates were fixed, _apply_overview_template() APPENDED the new correct sentence instead of REPLACING the old wrong one, leaving both wordings live simultaneously -- fixed via new _strip_existing_enterprise_sentences() helper wired into _apply_overview_template().

USER PUSHBACK (verbatim, free-text, not a preset option): after being shown two yaml.dump width tradeoffs (width=10000 collapses words' pre-wrapped fields; width=80 wraps cells' pre-unwrapped fields for the first time -- both semantically safe per round-trip + Hugo-render testing but cosmetically noisy in different directions) and asked to choose, the user said: "why are we doing it when both settings are not correct. what is the point" -- explicit rejection of a false-choice framing between two imperfect options for production-bound work. Correctly interpreted as an instruction to fix the actual root cause (full-document re-serialization touching unrelated fields), not tune a global parameter.

Built _surgical_replace_overview_content() (backlink_backfill.py, immediately before _rewrite_yaml_file()): locates the overview.content field's exact line span (handling both plain-scalar and |/> block-scalar styles) via a nested _block_end() helper, replaces ONLY that span with a freshly-serialized single-value fragment, optionally appends enterprise_backlink_injected as a new trailing line, returns None (never guesses) if the frontmatter structure does not match its narrow assumptions. Wired into backfill_products_yaml() write path as try-surgical-first: re-parses the result via yaml.safe_load() and verifies BOTH overview.content and enterprise_backlink_injected match exactly before trusting it; falls through unconditionally to the proven _rewrite_yaml_file() full-reserialization path on any mismatch/exception.

BUG #5, self-caught before presenting to the user (2026-08-22): the surgical patcher's marker-line insertion assumed a trailing single newline always meant a pre-existing BLANK line to insert before -- but a normal last line (no blank line before the closing ---, the common case, confirmed on cells' real frontmatter) also ends in exactly one newline. The old code stripped that single real newline and glued marker_line directly onto the prior line with ZERO separator, producing invalid YAML (verified via direct probe: _surgical_replace_overview_content() called standalone on the real cells file corrupted 'content_created_at: ...'+'enterprise_backlink_injected: ...' onto one line). This was silently caught EVERY TIME by backfill_products_yaml()'s own re-parse-and-verify safety net, which rejected the corrupt result and fell back to _rewrite_yaml_file() -- meaning the surgical path had never actually engaged in any of the real-file testing up to that point, even though the resulting diffs looked clean (cells/words happen to have no other multi-line fields that width=10000 reformatting would disturb, so the fallback path's output was coincidentally just as minimal). Fixed by replacing the conditional with an unconditional rstrip-then-reinsert (new_fm_text.rstrip newlines, then exactly one newline + marker_line + newline), which correctly collapses zero-or-more trailing blank lines into exactly one clean inserted line regardless of the original trailing structure.

VERIFICATION that the fix is real and the surgical path now genuinely engages (not just 'tests pass'): (a) 6 new dedicated unit tests added (TestSurgicalReplaceOverviewContent in test_backlink_backfill.py) covering plain-scalar style, block-literal style, no-overview-block fallback signal, no-content-key fallback signal, no-inject-url case, and body-preservation -- all pass. (b) Direct probe of _surgical_replace_overview_content() against the real, unmodified cells/_index.md file confirms it now returns valid, correctly-parseable YAML with content and enterprise_backlink_injected both landing exactly as intended. (c) DEFINITIVE proof of engagement: ran the real run_backfill() pipeline against cells+words with _rewrite_yaml_file (the fallback) monkeypatched to raise RuntimeError if ever called -- the run completed with total_modified=2, total_errors=0, producing the byte-identical clean diff seen in prior (fallback-masked) runs, proving the surgical path succeeds entirely on its own. (d) Hugo build of products.aspose.org with the corrected files in place renders the expected

paragraph correctly for both pages -- cells shows the new 'Enterprise Product Family' anchor text with zero remaining 'commercial edition' text; words shows its previously-missing backlink present with correct anchor text and URL. (e) Full regression suite: 725 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed (up from 719 pre-fix, +6 for the new surgical-patcher tests) -- scripts/pipeline/tests/ -k 'backlink or batch_reference'.

Content files reverted to clean HEAD state after every test cycle (git status --short confirms zero uncommitted changes to cells/_index.md or words/_index.md as of this record). No write+commit+push has occurred yet -- per Stage 1's own design ('Stop. Show the user the before/after diff... Wait for explicit approval before proceeding'), the clean canary diff is now ready to present to the user for explicit go-ahead before any real write+commit+push.
